_meta.indication: Adjunct to diet and exercise to improve glycemic control in adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus.

pivotal_trials.design: 52-week, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, 3-arm parallel group, multicenter trial; subjects randomized 1:1:1 to canagliflozin 100 mg, canagliflozin 300 mg, and matching placebo, with the primary efficacy analysis at 26 weeks.
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus inadequately controlled with diet and exercise (drug-naive or on single/low-dose oral antihyperglycemic therapy after washout).
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Change from baseline in HbA1c (%) at Week 26 versus placebo.
pivotal_trials.n: Main study arms: Cana 300 mg 193, Cana 100 mg 191, Placebo 189.
pivotal_trials.result: Placebo-subtracted HbA1c reduction: canagliflozin 300 mg -1.16% (95% CI -1.34, -0.99), p<.0001; canagliflozin 100 mg -0.91% (95% CI -1.09, -0.73), p<.0001.

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥5%): female genital mycotic infections (10.4% [100 mg] and 11.4% [300 mg] vs 3.2% placebo), urinary tract infection (5.9% and 4.3% vs 4.0%), and increased urination (5.3% and 4.6% vs 0.8%). Serious risks include hypotension/volume depletion and impairment in renal function (increased serum creatinine, decreased eGFR).
target_moa: Sodium glucose co-transporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitor that reduces glucose reabsorption in the proximal renal tubule, lowering hyperglycemia independent of insulin.

rems.type: No REMS required; identified safety risks are managed through labeling, including a Medication Guide.

advisory_committee.vote: Advisory committee held January 10, 2013; members voted 10 to 5 that the applicant provided sufficient efficacy and safety data to support marketing of canagliflozin for treatment of type 2 diabetes mellitus.

description.text: Added use of canagliflozin for initial therapy in combination with metformin

citations.quote: This Prior Approval sNDA, dated and received July 20, 2015, provides for addition of information to the labeling regarding use of canagliflozin for initial therapy in combination with metformin. This supplemental application also proposes changes to the labeling to comply with the Pregnancy and Lactation Labeling Rule (PLLR).

description.text: Added clinical data for canagliflozin as add-on combination therapy with metformin and a DPP-4 inhibitor

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental new drug application proposes to include new clinical data regarding add-on combination therapy with metformin and a dipeptidyl-peptidase-4 inhibitor to the prescribing information (PI), Section 14.2 Combination Therapy.

description.text: Added indication to reduce risk of major adverse cardiovascular events in adults with type 2 diabetes and established cardiovascular disease

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental new drug application provides for a new indication "to reduce the risk of major adverse cardiovascular events (cardiovascular death, nonfatal myocardial infarction and nonfatal stroke) in adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus and established cardiovascular disease (CVD)" for Invokana based on the results of studies 28431754DIA3008, entitled, "A Randomized, Multicenter, Double- Blind, Parallel, Placebo- Controlled Study of the Effects of JNJ-28431754 on Cardiovascular Outcomes in Adult Subjects with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus," (CANVAS) and 28431754DIA4003, entitled, "A Randomized, Multicenter, Double- Blind, Parallel, Placebo-Controlled Study of the Effects of Canagliflozin on Renal Endpoints in Adult Subjects with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus," (CANVAS-R).

description.text: Added indication to reduce the risk of ESKD, doubling of serum creatinine, CV death, and hospitalization for heart failure in adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus and diabetic nephropathy with albuminuria > 300 mg/day

citations.quote: The review team agrees that the application provides substantial evidence of canagliflozin's effectiveness in reducing the risk of end-stage kidney disease (ESKD), doubling of serum creatinine, cardiovascular (CV) death, and hospitalization for heart failure in adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus and diabetic nephropathy with albuminuria > 300 mg/day. The application will be approved for this new indication.

description.text: Removed Boxed Warning for Lower Limb Amputation and removed albuminuria condition for continued dosing in patients with eGFR 30 to <45 mL/min/1.73 m2

citations.quote: This Prior Approval sNDA provides for the removal from the Prescribing Information of the Boxed Warning for Lower Limb Amputation and the removal of the albuminuria condition for continued dosing of patients whose eGFR falls between 30 and less than 45 mL/min/1.73 m2.

description.text: Expanded type 2 diabetes indication to include pediatric patients aged 10 years and older

citations.quote: These Prior Approval sNDAs provide for the expansion of the approved indication as an adjunct to diet and exercise to improve glycemic control in adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus to include pediatric patients aged 10 years and older, with associated revisions to the Invokana, Invokamet, and Invokamet XR Prescribing Information and Medication Guides based on the results of the pediatric study 28431754DIA3018, entitled, *A Randomized, Multicenter, Double-Blind, Parallel-Group, Placebo-Controlled Study to Investigate the Efficacy and Safety of Canagliflozin in Children and Adolescents (\ge 10 to <18 years) with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus.*

summary.text: Canagliflozin (Invokana) was submitted as a 505(b)(1) NDA, received May 31, 2012, under standard review, and approved via a traditional (full) approval on the basis of nine Phase 3 glycemic efficacy trials, following a 10-to-5 favorable advisory committee vote; postmarketing requirements included deferred pediatric studies and a cardiovascular outcomes (MACE) trial.

Please see reviews of Drs. Kwon (clinical) and Liu (statistics) for details on the nine Phase 3 trials submitted in support of glycemic efficacy. Table 7.1 is adapted from Dr. Liu's review and summarizes the primary efficacy result in all these Phase 3 trials.

Overall, the committee members voted 10 to 5 on the question, "Based on the information included in the briefing materials and presentations today, has the applicant provided sufficient efficacy and safety data to support marketing of canagliflozin for the treatment of Type 2 diabetes mellitus?"

requirement.text: 2027-1: A clinical pharmacology study to evaluate the PK, PD, and safety of canagliflozin in pediatric patients ages 10 to <18 years with type 2 diabetes mellitus on metformin monotherapy (deferred pediatric study under PREA).

citations.quote: 2027-1 A clinical pharmacology study to evaluate the pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, and safety of canagliflozin in pediatric patients ages 10 to <18 years with type 2 diabetes mellitus on metformin monotherapy.

requirement.text: 2027-2: A 26-week randomized double-blind placebo-controlled study with a 26-week extension evaluating efficacy and safety of canagliflozin in pediatric patients ages 10 to <18 years with type 2 diabetes mellitus, as add-on to metformin and as monotherapy (deferred pediatric study).

citations.quote: 2027-2 A 26-week, randomized double-blind, placebo-controlled study, followed by a 26-week double-blind, placebo- or active-controlled extension, to evaluate the efficacy and safety of canagliflozin compared to placebo in pediatric patients ages 10 to <18 years with type 2 diabetes mellitus, as add-on to metformin and as monotherapy.

requirement.text: 2027-3: Enhanced pharmacovigilance (assessment/analysis of spontaneous reports) for malignancy (pheochromocytoma, Leydig cell tumor, renal cell carcinoma), fatal/hemorrhagic/necrotizing pancreatitis, severe hypersensitivity and photosensitivity reactions, serious hepatic abnormalities, and pregnancy, continuing 10 years for malignancies and 5 years for other events.

citations.quote: 2027-3 An assessment and analysis of all foreign and domestic spontaneous reports of malignancy (pheochromocytoma, Leydig cell tumor, and renal cell carcinoma), fatal pancreatitis, hemorrhagic/necrotizing pancreatitis, severe hypersensitivity reactions (angioedema, anaphylaxis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome), photosensitivity reactions, serious hepatic abnormalities, and pregnancy in patients treated with canagliflozin. The enhanced pharmacovigilance should continue for 10 years from the date of approval for malignancies and 5 years for all other events.

requirement.text: 2027-4: Completion and submission of the final report for the 78-week double-blind extension phase of DIA3010 to assess long-term safety including effects on bone mineral density and bone turnover markers.

citations.quote: 2027-4 Completion and submission of the final report for the 78-week double-blind extension phase of DIA3010, a clinical trial to assess the long-term safety of canagliflozin, including, but not limited to, the effect of the addition of canagliflozin to the addition of placebo on bone mineral density and markers of bone turnover.

requirement.text: 2027-5: A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial evaluating the effect of canagliflozin on the incidence of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus, to show the upper bound of the 2-sided 95% CI of the MACE risk ratio is less than 1.3.

citations.quote: 2027-5 A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial evaluating the effect of canagliflozin on the incidence of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus. The primary objective of the trial should be to demonstrate that the upper bound of the 2-sided 95% confidence interval for the estimated risk ratio comparing the incidence of MACE (non-fatal myocardial infarction, non-fatal stroke, cardiovascular death) observed with canagliflozin to that observed in the placebo group is less than 1.3.
